title: Krull topology on the fixing subgroup of a finite intermediate field
statement: Let K be a field [def-pc-field-extension], Ks a separable closure of K [def-pd-separable-closure], and L an intermediate field of Ks/K that is finite-dimensional over K. Equip Gal(Ks/K) and Gal(Ks/L) with their Krull topologies, and L.fixingSubgroup with the subspace topology from Gal(Ks/K). The canonical multiplicative equivalence L.fixingSubgroupEquiv : L.fixingSubgroup ≃* Gal(Ks/L), which retains the underlying automorphism of Ks, is continuous in both directions.

proof.text: For a basic identity neighborhood in Gal(Ks/L), choose a finite intermediate extension E/L whose fixing subgroup lies in it. E is finite-dimensional over K by the tower theorem. The identity K-linear map transfers this finiteness to E.restrictScalars K. Its fixing subgroup is open in Gal(Ks/K), so intersecting with L.fixingSubgroup gives an open neighborhood mapped into the original neighborhood. The homomorphism continuity-at-one criterion proves continuity of fixingSubgroupEquiv.

The domain is a closed subgroup of the compact group Gal(Ks/K), hence compact. Ks/L is algebraic by separability in the tower, so Gal(Ks/L) is Hausdorff. Apply Continuous.continuous_symm_of_equiv_compact_to_t2 to the underlying bijection to prove inverse continuity.
